detailed_rationale:
Suzlon enters FY27 running the best commercial cadence of its 30-year history, and the turnaround arc is now well past 'stabilization' into genuine execution. The balance sheet is nil-debt as of 31 March 2026 (consolidated net worth Rs 9,464 crore, net cash Rs 2,384 crore) -- a stunning reversal from negative net worth of Rs -3,526 crore in FY22, achieved through the 2019-2020 debt restructuring, repeated equity infusions (promoter holding is now diluted to just 11.71% as of the June-2026 quarter, with promoter pledge at a clean 0.0%, per Trendlyne's shareholding tracker) and, critically, actual operating cash generation since FY23. On the commercial side, the order book has compounded from a mere 0.65 GW (Mar-2023) to 2.93 GW (Mar-2024) to 5.9 GW at FY26-close (66% PSU+C&I) to a fresh ~6.4 GW / 1.9x book-to-bill by mid-2026 on continued repeat wins (a 195 MW repeat order and a 204.75 MW Jindal Renewables C&I expansion in May 2026, a 400 MW Tata Power Renewable EPC order), and the flagship S144 (3 MW-class) platform has crossed roughly 9 GW of cumulative platform sales, evidence the product itself -- not just balance-sheet repair -- is winning share. Execution has followed: FY26 deliveries hit a record 2,456 MW (Q4 alone 830 MW), driving 54% revenue growth to Rs 16,679 crore and 63% EBITDA growth to Rs 3,022 crore (18.1% margin, +100bps YoY); sell-side models roughly 3.1 GW of FY27 deliveries (+26% YoY), consistent with management's own sector call of 8 GW of national wind installations in FY27 and 10 GW in FY28 (versus roughly 6+ GW in FY26 and under 1.5 GW as recently as FY22) -- Suzlon has captured a large, arguably outsized, share of that recovery given ALMM (Wind)'s new localization mandate (blade/tower/gearbox/generator/bearing assembly must sit in India, per MNRE's July-2026 ALMM clarifications) plays directly to Suzlon's fully in-house manufacturing versus import-dependent rivals.

Earnings quality is where this name needs real scrutiny, and it is the crux of why the quant model's 22.3x trailing PE (which our own mcap/PAT check of Rs 70,850cr / Rs 3,162cr reproduces almost exactly, confirming the quant snapshot's PE=22.3 is computed off headline, not normalized, PAT) understates the true multiple. We pulled Suzlon's PIT quarterly file directly (unified_quarterly_pit.parquet, 26 rows for SUZLON, available_date-sequenced) and it independently confirms two things reported in the press: FY26 PBT summed across the four quarters (459+562+567+833) = Rs 2,421 crore versus reported PBT of Rs 2,422 crore, and FY26 net profit summed (324+1,279+445+1,114) = Rs 3,162 crore versus reported PAT of Rs 3,153-3,163 crore (source-dependent) -- i.e., a net tax CREDIT of roughly Rs 741 crore for the year, matching the company's own disclosed 'deferred tax asset recognition of Rs 742 crore.' Crucially, our PIT pull shows this was not a single Q4 one-off: the tax_pct field is deeply negative in Q2 FY26 (-127%, net profit Rs 1,279cr on PBT of only Rs 562cr) and again in Q4 FY26 (-34%), and FY25 shows the same pattern in Q4 FY25 (-114%, the Rs 638 crore DTA credit disclosed alongside FY25's 'decade-high' PBT of Rs 1,447cr and PAT of Rs 2,072cr). Two consecutive fiscal years of large, multi-quarter tax credits is a recurring pattern, not an isolated one-off gain the way ABB's Robotics-divestment gain was -- it reflects the phased recognition of a large legacy pool of carried-forward tax losses from Suzlon's 2012-2022 near-insolvency years, and it is a genuine future cash-tax shield (real value), not merely an accounting fiction. But it does mean headline PAT growth has been running well ahead of PBT growth, and will likely decelerate below PBT growth in any year the recognition pace slows even if the underlying business keeps compounding -- an expectations trap for anyone anchoring on trailing EPS. Applying a standard ~25.17% effective tax rate to FY26 PBT of Rs 2,421cr gives a normalized PAT of roughly Rs 1,812cr, and a normalized trailing PE of Rs 70,850cr / Rs 1,812cr = approximately 39x -- nearly 1.7x the quant model's headline 22.3x. Layered on top of that, the revenue mix is shifting toward EPC (27% of order book now, versus 20% in Sep-2025, targeting 50% by FY28), and EPC/government-PSU tenders carry structurally lower gross margins (roughly 8-12%) and far longer receivable cycles (DISCOM-linked payment lags pushing consolidated receivable days toward ~130) than pure C&I wind-turbine supply (15-20% gross margin, faster-paying private counterparties) -- a real, ongoing dilution to blended margin even as volumes scale.

On valuation, a ~39x normalized multiple is defensible only if the current order-book visibility (6.4 GW backlog against Rs 16,679cr trailing revenue is roughly 2.4 years of revenue in hand -- respectable but nowhere near an L&T-style multi-year EPC backlog) converts into sustained 20%+ compounding for several more years, which the sector call (8 GW FY27, 10 GW FY28 installations, RPO-turned-RCO mandates rising to 33.01% in FY26 and 35.95% in FY27) makes plausible but not certain: RPO/RCO enforcement has historically been patchy (only 6 of 24 audited states actually imposed penalties for shortfalls), and the phased ISTS-charge-waiver withdrawal for wind projects (25% of full charges for Jul-2025-Jun-2026 COD, rising to 50% the following year and full charges by 2028) is a genuine, rising cost headwind on Suzlon's own developer-customers' project IRRs that could eventually cool order placement, even if it hasn't yet. Layer in the company's own scar tissue -- a decade of CDR restructuring, negative net worth as recently as FY22, and equity dilution that has left founding promoters at just 11.71% of the register -- and the market's residual credibility discount on this name (a multiple below what the raw ROE/ROCE profile of 33.4%/30.2% would otherwise command) looks earned rather than irrational, even as the underlying business has genuinely turned the corner.
recommendation_rationale: Hold, not Sell, and in line with the quant model's own Hold verdict on both the 3-year and 1-year horizons -- but this Hold is more finely balanced than the quant screen's headline PE (22.3x) suggests. The case against selling: the balance sheet is genuinely nil-debt with a clean net-cash position, the order book has compounded for ten consecutive quarters (0.65 GW to ~6.4 GW), FY26 execution was a real record (2,456 MW delivered, 54% revenue growth, margin expansion to 18.1%), and ALMM localization plus rising RCO mandates are structural, not cyclical, tailwinds that favor Suzlon's fully domestic manufacturing footprint specifically. There is no balance-sheet or governance red flag (zero pledge, deleveraged), and the quality/value percentile scores (92.9/77.8) reflect a real, not manufactured, improvement in the franchise. The case against adding fresh capital or treating this as a comfortable Hold: our own reconstruction of the tax line (cross-verified against the internal PIT parquet, not just press reports) shows the reported 22.3x PE is a genuinely misleading anchor -- normalized for a standard tax rate, the multiple is closer to 39x, nearly double, and that gap is exactly the kind of distortion that can silently support an over-generous quant Value score (SUZLON's value_score_pctile of 77.8 likely embeds this same undertaxed-PAT effect). At a true ~39x, the market needs Suzlon to sustain 20%+ compounding for several more years merely to hold the current price, against a backdrop of EPC-mix margin dilution, patchy RPO/RCO enforcement, a rising ISTS-waiver cost headwind for customers, and a promoter base so diluted (11.71%) that it has limited skin left in the register. Net: hold the existing position -- the fundamental turnaround is real and the order book supports continued growth -- but do not mistake the quant model's 22.3x for the real multiple, and treat two consecutive quarters of PBT growth stalling below ~15% YoY, or EPC mix crossing 40% without an offsetting margin lever, as the trigger to revisit toward Sell.
summary: Suzlon's operational turnaround is real: nil consolidated debt, a 6.4 GW order book built from essentially zero three years ago (66% PSU+C&I), record FY26 deliveries of 2,456 MW, 54% revenue growth and margin expansion to 18.1% EBITDA, all riding a genuine sector tailwind (national wind installations guided to 8 GW FY27 / 10 GW FY28, ALMM localization favoring Suzlon's in-house manufacturing). But the quant snapshot's 22.3x trailing PE is a headline artifact: our own reconstruction from the internal PIT quarterly file (26 rows, FY26 quarters summing exactly to the reported Rs 2,421cr PBT / Rs 3,162cr PAT) confirms a recurring, multi-quarter deferred-tax-asset credit (Rs 742cr in FY26 after Rs 638cr in FY25) that inflates headline PAT by roughly 40% above a standard-tax-rate normalized figure -- the true multiple is closer to 39x, not 22x, and that gap likely also overstates SUZLON's 77.8th-percentile Value score in the quant model. Against that truer multiple, sustaining the current price needs several more years of 20%+ growth, which the order book and sector tailwind can plausibly support but which EPC-mix margin dilution (target 50% EPC by FY28 versus 27% now, lower-margin than pure WTG supply), patchy RPO/RCO enforcement, a phasing-in ISTS transmission-charge headwind for wind-project developers, and a decade-long credibility overhang (promoter stake diluted to 11.71%, though pledge is a clean 0%) all argue for some caution rather than complacency. Call: Hold.
positive_para: The balance sheet turnaround is complete and clean: nil consolidated debt as of 31-Mar-2026, net cash of Rs 2,384 crore, net worth of Rs 9,464 crore (from -Rs 3,526 crore in FY22), and a promoter pledge of exactly 0.0% as of the June-2026 quarter (Trendlyne) -- no governance red flag despite the historically diluted 11.71% promoter stake. Commercially, the order book has compounded for ten straight quarters from 0.65 GW (Mar-2023) to roughly 6.4 GW with a 1.9x book-to-bill by mid-2026, on the back of repeat wins (195 MW repeat order, a 204.75 MW Jindal Renewables C&I expansion, a 400 MW Tata Power Renewable EPC order, all announced May-Jun 2026), and the flagship S144 (3 MW-class) platform has crossed roughly 9 GW of cumulative sales -- genuine product-market fit, not just book-keeping recovery. Execution has followed the order book: FY26 deliveries hit a record 2,456 MW (Q4 alone 830 MW, itself a record quarter), driving 54% revenue growth to Rs 16,679 crore and 63% EBITDA growth to Rs 3,022 crore (18.1% margin, +100bps YoY), with sell-side modeling roughly 3.1 GW of FY27 deliveries (+26% YoY). The policy backdrop is a structural, not cyclical, tailwind specific to Suzlon: MNRE's ALMM (Wind) framework (formerly RLMM) now mandates that blade, tower, gearbox, generator and special-bearing manufacturing sit in India for Type Certification -- components that are 65-70% of turbine cost -- directly favoring Suzlon's fully in-house manufacturing versus import-dependent competitors, while national wind installations are guided to grow from roughly 6 GW (FY26) to 8 GW (FY27) and 10 GW (FY28) and rising Renewable Consumption Obligation (RCO, successor to RPO) mandates (33.01% in FY26, 35.95% in FY27, wind-specific sub-obligation doubling to 1.6%) add a policy-driven demand floor.
negative_para: The headline 22.3x trailing PE materially understates the true multiple because of a large, recurring, multi-quarter deferred-tax-asset credit that our own pull of the internal PIT quarterly parquet (26 rows for SUZLON) independently confirms: FY26 PBT of Rs 2,421 crore against net profit of Rs 3,162 crore (a Rs 741cr tax credit, negative effective tax rate in 2 of 4 FY26 quarters, most sharply Q2 FY26 at -127%), following an essentially identical pattern in FY25 (Rs 638cr DTA credit, PAT of Rs 2,072cr against PBT of only Rs 1,447cr). This is the phased recognition of a legacy carry-forward-loss pool from Suzlon's 2012-2022 near-insolvency years -- a real future cash-tax shield, but one that has inflated two consecutive years of headline PAT growth well above underlying PBT growth, meaning reported PAT growth will likely undershoot the business's real operating growth in any year the recognition pace slows. Applying a standard ~25.17% tax rate to FY26 PBT gives a normalized PAT of roughly Rs 1,812cr and a normalized PE of approximately 39x -- nearly double the quant model's 22.3x -- and this same undertaxed-PAT effect likely inflates SUZLON's 77.8th-percentile Value score. Layered on top, the revenue mix is shifting toward lower-margin EPC (27% of order book now versus 20% in Sep-2025, targeting 50% by FY28), and government/PSU-linked orders (66% of the 5.9-6.4 GW book) carry both lower gross margins (8-12% vs 15-20% for C&I) and much longer DISCOM-linked receivable cycles (consolidated receivable days near 130) than private C&I customers -- a structural drag on both margin and working capital as the PSU-heavy backlog executes. Policy tailwinds are real but not unconditional: RPO/RCO enforcement has historically been weak (only 6 of 24 audited states penalized shortfalls), and the phased withdrawal of the ISTS transmission-charge waiver for wind projects (25% of full charges for Jul-2025-Jun-2026 commissioning, rising to 100% by 2028) is a genuine, rising cost headwind on developer-customer project economics. And the company's own history -- a decade of debt restructuring, negative net worth as recently as FY22, and equity dilution that has left promoters at just 11.71% -- means the market's residual valuation discount versus the raw 33.4% ROE / 30.2% ROCE profile likely reflects earned skepticism, not pure mispricing.
reverse_dcf_judgment: The quant snapshot's 22.3x trailing PE reproduces cleanly from mcap (Rs 70,850cr, 17-Jul-2026) divided by reported FY26 PAT (Rs 3,162cr, itself cross-verified against the internal PIT parquet) -- but that reported PAT includes a Rs 741cr net tax credit tied to phased recognition of legacy carried-forward tax losses, the second consecutive year of such a credit (Rs 638cr in FY25). Normalizing FY26 PBT (Rs 2,421cr) at a standard ~25.17% effective tax rate gives a normalized PAT of roughly Rs 1,812cr and a normalized trailing PE of approximately 39x -- the more honest anchor for a reverse-DCF read, since the tax-credit tailwind is real but will eventually fade toward a normal effective rate once the legacy NOL pool is exhausted (undisclosed remaining pool size is a genuine data gap here). At ~39x normalized earnings against 33.4%/30.2% ROE/ROCE, the market is pricing sustained mid-20s%-plus annualized earnings growth for several years, or an implicit re-rating premium for balance-sheet-repair/scarcity value similar to what we flagged in ABB's case -- not a re-run of the trailing 41-53% revenue growth prints, which were themselves flattered by an extremely low FY22-23 base coming out of near-insolvency and cannot be extrapolated. The order book (6.4 GW, ~2.4 years of trailing revenue) and sector guidance (8 GW FY27, 10 GW FY28 installations) can plausibly support 20-25% compounding for the next two to three years, which would make the current multiple full-but-not-indefensible -- but EPC-mix dilution, patchy RPO/RCO enforcement, and the ISTS-waiver phase-out are real drags on both the growth rate and the multiple the market should be willing to pay for it. Our honest read: priced for continued strong execution with limited room for a growth disappointment, not for a business in structural decline, but also not screening nearly as cheap as the quant model's 22.3x implies once the tax-credit distortion is stripped out.
escalation_reason: Methodology gap, not a data-staleness issue: SUZLON's headline trailing PE (22.3x, reproduced exactly from mcap/reported-PAT) and its 77.8th-percentile Value score are both computed off reported PAT that includes a large, recurring, multi-quarter deferred-tax-asset credit (Rs 742cr in FY26, Rs 638cr in FY25 -- independently confirmed against the internal PIT quarterly parquet, 26 rows, FY26 quarterly PBT/PAT summing to the exact reported annual figures). Normalizing PAT for a standard ~25.17% tax rate lifts the true multiple to roughly 39x -- nearly double the headline screen -- which would meaningfully change how 'cheap' this name looks on any PE- or earnings-yield-based factor in the 750-universe screen. This is the second name in this review cycle where a non-recurring or non-cash-tax item has been found to distort the headline PE/Value read (ABB's Q1 CY2026 divestment gain was the first, flagged in that review without escalation since it was a clean one-off); SUZLON's version is structurally different and arguably more persistent -- it stems from a real, multi-year legacy NOL pool being recognized in installments, not a single transaction -- and is a pattern likely to recur in ANY other post-restructuring/post-CDR name in the 750 universe still working through legacy carried-forward losses (e.g., other companies that went through 2012-2022-era debt restructuring). Recommend Arjun Rao's quant desk consider a normalized-PAT (standard effective tax rate) adjustment, or at minimum a flag, for any stock where reported tax_pct is negative or the PAT/PBT ratio exceeds ~1.0x in the trailing four quarters, before that name's PE/Value percentile is used for screening or allocation.

technical_commentary: The big story here is already behind it: a roughly 14x run from 2021 to a September-2024 peak (80), followed by nearly two years of range-bound consolidation (trailing 12 months confined to roughly 40-59) with a genuinely tangled 10/20/40-month average stack (no clean ordering) and a sub-40% higher-high hit rate over the trailing two years. Volume has stayed elevated rather than drying up during this base, which is atypical for constructive consolidation -- this reads as an extended, undecided range rather than a base poised to break out.
